However, the signature of the orbital humps (or a hot spot) was far less prominently observed in the orbital light curves and eclipse profiles than in usual dwarf novae with similar orbital periods. The combination of a low frequency of outbursts and an apparent lack of slowly rising, long outbursts in GY Cnc is difficult to reconcile within the standard framework of dwarf novae. We suspect that GY Cnc may be the first above-the-gap counterpart of the unusual eclipsing dwarf novae HT Cas and IR Com.

articleTitle: Roche Potential with Luminous Accretion Disks
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: The radiative environments of an interacting binary, which contains a luminous accretion disk, are investigated. The disk radiation field has no effect in the direction of the orbital plane, while it significantly affects in the polar direction. As the disk luminosity increases, the Roche potential around the compact star becomes hollow in the polar direction. It further crashes toward the pole, and a cone of avoidance appears at the normalized luminosity <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma_{\rm d} \equiv L_{\rm d}/L_{\rm E} =0.5$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_{\rm d}$</tex> is the disk luminosity and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_{\rm E}$</tex> the Eddington luminosity of the compact star. The disk corona, the wind-fed accretion flow, and the common envelope suffer a remarkable influence by the luminous disk in active binaries. Of these, the wind-fed accretion is briefly discussed.

articleTitle: Are Jets Ejected from Locally Magnetized Accretion Disks?
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We investigated the jet formation from accretion disks in which a weak localized poloidal magnetic field is initially embedded. Previous MHD numerical simulations of jet formation from accretion disks initially assumed a large-scale vertical uniform magnetic field that threads the disk, which showed that jets are ejected from accretion disks by a magneto-centrifugal force and magnetic pressure. In contrast to a large-scale uniform magnetic field, what happens if the magnetic field is localized in the disk? Our MHD numerical simulation shows that the jet structure appears even if the initial magnetic field is localized in the disk. The disk material is ejected as a poloidal magnetic loop by magnetic pressure due to a toroidal magnetic field that is generated by the disk rotation. Though the ejection mechanism is different from that of the magneto-centrifugally driven jet model, the rising magnetic loop behaves like a jet; it is collimated by a pinching force of the toroidal magnetic field, and its velocity is on order of the Keplerian velocity of the disk.

articleTitle: Dwarf Nova-Like Outburst of Short-Period Intermediate Polar HT Camelopardalis
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report on the first time-series observations of a short outburst of the proposed intermediate polar HT Cam (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$=$</tex> RX J0757.0<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+$</tex>6306). On 2001 December 29, we detected that the object was undergoing a bright outburst at a magnitude of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m_{\rm vis} = 12.2$</tex>. Following this detection, we started international joint observations through VSNET. The light curve showed a gradual decline for the first 0.5 d. Following this short plateau phase, the rate of decline dramatically increased to more than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4 \,{\rm mag} \,{\rm d}^{-1}$</tex>. Within 1.5 d from the outburst detection, the object almost declined to the quiescent level. During the rapidly declining phase, long-term modulations with a period of 86min and strong pulses with a period of 8.6 min were observed. We concluded that 86 min and 8.6 min are the orbital period and the spin period of HT Cam, respectively. By detecting the spin period, we confirmed the IP classification of HT Cam. However, its outburst behavior rather resembles that of dwarf novae. The discrepancy between the declining rates of the total flux and the pulse flux strongly suggests that disk instabilities took place during the outburst.

articleTitle: Asymmetrical Distribution of Sunspot Groups in the Solar Hemispheres
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: In the present work, the north–south asymmetry of solar activity was examined by analyzing statistically the hemispheric distribution of annual numbers of sunspot groups, using the Royal Greenwich Observatory data set from the year 1874 through 2000. An interesting phenomenon is found that the solar activity of a cycle usually has the same beginning and end times, but different maximum amplitudes at different maximum times in the hemispheres. Some characteristics of the asymmetry of solar activity were investigated and explained. For solar cycle 23, a dominance of solar activity is predicted to occur in the southern hemisphere in several forthcoming years.

articleTitle: On the Origin of Early Superhumps in WZ Sge-Type Stars
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: The origin of early superhumps, which are double-wave periodic modulations seen only during the earliest stage of a WZ Sge-type outburst, has not been well understood. Based on a recent discovery of two-armed arch-like patterns on Doppler tomograms in conjunction with early superhumps, we propose a new interpretation on the origin of early superhumps, following a new interpretation by Smak (2001, Acta Astron., 51, 295) and Ogilvie (2002, MNRAS, 330, 937) of the two-armed pattern seen in IP Peg. If we consider irradiation of the elevated surface of the accretion disk caused by vertical tidal deformation, we can consistently explain the observed features on Doppler tomograms and photometric waves at the same time. We interpret that a combination of low mass-ratios (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex>) and low mass-transfer rates, necessary to give rise to these tidal effects, discriminate WZ Sge-type stars from other SU UMa-type dwarf novae. Based on recent fluid calculations, such an effect would be observable in higher <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex> systems. We interpret that RZ Leo is an example of such objects.

articleTitle: IR Com: Deeply Eclipsing Dwarf Nova Below the Period Gap —A Twin of HT Cas?
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We observed an X-ray selected, deeply eclipsing cataclysmic variable IR Com (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$=\rm{S}~10932$</tex>). We detected an outburst occurring on 1996 January 1. The light curve of the outburst closely resembled that of a normal outburst of an SU UMa-type dwarf nova, rather than that of an intermediate polar. Time-resolved photometry during the outburst showed that eclipses became systematically deeper and narrower as the outburst faded. Full-orbit light curves in quiescence showed little evidence of orbital humps or asymmetry of the eclipses. In addition to the presence of high–low transitions in quiescence, the overall behavior of the outbursts and the characteristics of the eclipse profiles suggest that IR Com can be best understood as a twin of HT Cas, a famous eclipsing SU UMa-type dwarf nova with a number of peculiarities.

articleTitle: A Deep Optical Observation for an Enigmatic Unidentified Gamma-Ray Source 3EG J1835+5918
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report on a deep optical imaging observation using the Subaru Telescope for a very soft X-ray source, RX J1836.2<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+$</tex>5925, which has been suspected to be an isolated neutron star associated with the brightest as-yet unidentified EGRET source outside the Galactic plane, 3EG J1835<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+$</tex>5918. An extended source having a complex, bipolar shape is found at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B\sim 26$</tex>, which might be an extended pulsar nebular whose flux is about 5–6 orders of magnitude lower than gamma-ray flux, although finding a galaxy of this magnitude by chance in the error circle is of order unity. We have found two even fainter, possible point sources at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B \sim 28$</tex>, although their detections are not firm because of a low signal-to-noise ratio. If the extended object of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B\sim 26$</tex> is a galaxy and not related to 3EG J1835<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+$</tex>5918, a lower limit on the X-ray/optical flux ratio can be set as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_{\rm X}/f_B \gtrsim 2700$</tex>, giving further strong support for the neutron-star identification of 3EG J1835<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+$</tex>5918. Interestingly, if either of the two sources at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B \sim 28$</tex> is the real counterpart of RX J1836.2<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+$</tex>5925 and thermal emission from the surface of an isolated neutron star, the temperature and distance to the source become <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 4 \times 10^5 \,{\rm K}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 300 \,{\rm pc}$</tex>, respectively, showing a striking similarity of its spectral energy distribution to the proto-type radio-quiet gamma-ray pulsar Geminga. No detection of nonthermal hard X-ray emission is consistent with the ASCA upper limit, if the nonthermal flux of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\hbox{3EG J1835$+$5918} / \hbox{RX J1836.2$+$5925}$</tex> 3EG J1835<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+$</tex>5918<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$/$</tex>RX J1836.2<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+$</tex>5925 is at a similar level to that of Geminga.

articleTitle: Search for Hot Gas in the Local Group with ASCA
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: An X-ray study was made to examine whether some part of the soft X-ray background is coming from hot gas in the Local Group. For this purpose, four consecutive pointings were made with ASCA toward a sky region between M31 and M33, which is close to the direction of the center of the Local Group. By comparing the X-ray surface brightness in this sky direction with that in another blank sky region near the north equatorial pole, an upper limit on any soft excess X-ray background was determined to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.8 \times 10^{-9} \,\rm{erg} \,\rm{cm}^{-2} \,\rm{s}^{-1} \,\rm{sr}^{-1}$</tex> with a 90% confidence level statistical error. Assuming an optically-thin thermal bremsstrahlung energy spectrum (Raymond–Smith model) for a temperature of 1 keV and a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta$</tex>-model electron density distribution for a core radius of 100 kpc for the X-ray halo, the upper limit of the central plasma density was obtained to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.3 \times 10^{-4} \,\rm{cm}^{-3}$</tex>. The plasma column density is too low to contribute significantly to the observed quadrupole anisotropy in the cosmic microwave background.

articleTitle: Detections of SiO Masers from the Large-Amplitude Variables in the Galactic Nuclear Disk
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We have surveyed known large-amplitude variables within <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$15'$</tex> of the Galactic center in the SiO <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J=1 \hbox{-} 0$</tex><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v=1$</tex> and 2 maser lines at 43 GHz, resulting in 79 detections and 58 non-detections. The detection rate of 58 percent is comparable to that obtained in Bulge IRAS source surveys. SiO lines were also detected from four other sources near the program objects. The SiO detection rate increases steeply with the period, particularly for stars with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P \gt 500 \,{\rm d}$</tex><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P \gt 500 \,{\rm d}$</tex>, where it exceeds 80%. We found at a given period that the SiO detection rate is approximately double that for OH. These facts suggest that the large-amplitude variables in the Nuclear Disk region are AGB stars similar in their overall properties to the inner and outer bulge IRAS/SiO sources.

articleTitle: The 1999 Optical Outburst of the Fast X-Ray Nova, V4641 Sagittarii
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report on the detection of an optical outburst which preceded the X-ray main flare of the fast X-ray nova V4641 Sagittarii. The object became active since early August 1999, and then experienced an optical outburst reaching 8.8 mag on 1999 September 15. The observed maximum was between two X-ray flares, that is, 12.1 hr after the X-ray sub-flare and 7.4 hr before the main one. The brightness returned to the quiescent level within 5 d, which indicates that the optical outburst rapidly faded as those at other wavelengths, while typical X-ray novae exponentially decay with an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$e$</tex>-folding time of 30–40 d. We confirmed ellipsoidal modulations in our observations at quiescence. Using them with the previously reported observations, we calculated the period of modulations to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.817284\pm 0.000018 \,\rm{d}$</tex>. From the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm{H}\alpha$</tex> absorption line in quiescent spectra, we obtained the semi-amplitude of the radial velocity for the secondary star to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$176 \pm 20 \,\rm{km} \,\rm{s}^{-1}$</tex>. Assuming the mass ratio reported in Orosz et al. (2001, ApJ, 555, 489) we estimated the lower limit of the compact object mass to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5.84 \,{{{M}_{\odot}}}$</tex>. To interpret the short outburst and the large luminosity during the outburst, we propose a scenario of a transient supercritical accretion onto a black hole.

articleTitle: Polarization in Blazars
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Based on the beaming model, a relation between the observed polarization and the Doppler factor was obtained by Fan et al. (, AAA068.159.190), who showed that the polarization is associated with the Doppler factor (boosting factor) in BL Lacertae objects (BLs). Polarization and Doppler factors have also been obtained for some optically violently variable quasars (OVVs). Do OVVs also fit a similar relation to that of BLs? In the present Letter, BLs and OVVs are plotted in a polarization–Doppler factor diagram. The results indicate that OVVs follow a similar polarization–Doppler factor relation as the BLs, and that the parameter <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex>, the ratio of the beamed luminosity to the unbeamed luminosity in the source frame for BLs, is greater than that for OVVs. This result suggests that the polarization mechanism in the two subclasses of active galactic nuclei is the same. The difference in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex> means the intrinsic polarization in OVVs is lower than that in BLs. The boosted emissions in BLs dominate the unbeamed emissions, and therefore the emission lines in BLs are weak or invisible, which is consistent with observations.

articleTitle: SPH Simulations of Spiral Shocks in Discs around Black Holes
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Spiral structures and shocks often appear in astrophysical gas dynamics and particular in accretion-disc simulations; however, they are difficult to follow numerically. In this paper we consider a black hole of 8<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${M}_{\odot}$</tex> as a primary and a small secondary of 0.5 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${M}_{\odot}$</tex>, following the idea that a low <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M_{2}/M_{1}$</tex> would favour spiral structure and possibly spiral shock onset through gas compression induced by strong gravitational attraction. In the framework of Smooth Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH), we performed two 2D models and two 3D models. Simulations in either pair are distinguished by the adopted <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma$</tex> value (low and high compressibility cases). Indeed, both 2D models reveal the existence of spiral structures in the disc bulk. Furthermore, spiral shocks at the outer disc edge are evident for the high compressibility 2D model. Spiral structures appear to develop also for the 3D high compressibility model. Instead, for the 3D low compressibility model, no clear conclusion can be drawn as the number of particles (and thus the SPH resolution) is low.

articleTitle: Emission-Line Eclipse Mapping of Velocity Fields in a Dwarf-Nova Accretion Disk
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We propose a new method, emission-line eclipse mapping, to map the velocity fields of an accretion disk in position space. Quiescent dwarf novae usually exhibit double-peaked emission-line profiles because of disk rotation. Since a part of a disk having a different line-of-sight velocity is successively obscured by a companion in eclipsing systems, they show time-varying line profiles. We calculated the time changes of the emission-line profiles, assuming Keplerian rotation fields (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v_\varphi\propto r^{-1/2}$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r$</tex> being the distance from the disk center) and an emissivity distribution of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$j \propto r^{-3/2}$</tex>. We, then, applied the usual eclipse mapping technique to the light curves at each of 12–24 wavelengths across the line center to map the region with the same line-of-sight velocity. The reconstructed images typically exhibit a ‘two-eye’ pattern for high line-of-sight velocities, and we can recover the relation, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v_\varphi \propto d^{-1/2}$</tex>, on the assumption of an axisymmetric disk, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex> is the separation between the two ‘eyes’. We will be able to probe the Keplerian rotation law, the most fundamental assumption adopted in many disk models, by high-speed spectroscopic observations with 8-m class telescopes.

articleTitle: Detection of Water Maser Flare in the Seyfert/LINER, NGC 6240
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report on a flare-up of water-vapor maser emission in a prototypical ultraluminous FIR galaxy with an AGN, NGC 6240. The flux density of the detected maser line was <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\approx 0.1 \,{\rm Jy}$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$FWHM {\approx 5} \,{\rm km} \,{\rm s}^{-1}$</tex>, indicating an apparent isotropic luminosity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\approx 100 \,{L}_{\odot}$</tex> at a distance of 100 Mpc, which is typical for water megamasers. The maser line was redshifted by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\approx 200 \,{\rm km} \,{\rm s}^{-1}$</tex> relative to the systemic velocity of the galaxy, while no systemic-velocity feature was detected. The previous possible detection or observed upper limits were at a level lower than the flux density in the present paper, indicating that the water maser in NGC 6240 flared up by more than a factor of 5 in 2001.

articleTitle: Spiral Structure in WZ Sagittae around the 2001 Outburst Maximum
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Intermediate-resolution phase-resolved spectra of WZ Sge were obtained on five consecutive nights (July 23–27) covering the initial stage of the 2001 superoutburst. Double-peaked emission lines of He II at 4686 Å, which were absent on July 23, emerged on July 24 together with emission lines of C III <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$/$</tex> N III Bowen blend. Analyses of the He II emission lines using the Doppler tomography revealed an asymmetric spiral structure on the accretion disk. This finding demonstrates that spiral shocks with a very short orbital period can arise during the initial stage of an outburst and may be present in all SU UMa stars.

articleTitle: A New Test for the Absorption Mechanism of GPS Radio Sources Using Polarization Properties
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We consider the use of polarization properties as a means to discriminate between Synchrotron Self-Absorption (SSA) and Free–Free Absorption (FFA) in GHz-Peaked Spectrum (GPS) sources. The polarization position angle (PA) of synchrotron radiation at high frequencies for the optically thin regime is perpendicular to the magnetic field, whereas it is parallel to the magnetic field at low frequencies for the optically thick regime. Therefore, SSA produces a change in PA of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$90^{\circ}$</tex> across the spectral peak, while FFA does not result in such a change. We analyzed polarization data from VLA observations for six GPS sources to see if such a change in PA was present. Our results indicate that there is no significant evidence for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$90^{\circ}$</tex> change in PA across the spectral peak, suggesting that FFA is more likely than SSA for low-frequency cutoffs in these sources.

articleTitle: Effects of Relativistic Expansion on Late-Time Supernova Light Curves
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: The effects of relativistic expansion on late-time supernova (SN) light curves (LCs) were investigated, and an analytic expression for a correction term to the (quasi-)exponential decay was obtained. It has been shown that the relativistic effects brighten the LC owing to (1) a delayed decay of radioactive nuclei (time-dilation) as well as to (2) Lorentz boosting of the photon energies. The leading correction term is quadratic in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta$</tex> is the maximum velocity of ejecta divided by the speed of light, and grows as a quadratic function of time. Thus, the relativistic effect is negligibly small at early times, but becomes of considerable size at late times. It was also shown that including the differential time-dilation effect is essential for an accurate LC prediction better than to first order in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta$</tex>. For ordinary SNe, the effect is too small to be detected. However, in SNe having a very large energy (hypernovae) or exploding in an aspherical geometry, radioactive <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{56\atop} \rm{Ni}}$</tex> is likely to be boosted to higher velocities. We might then see an appreciable excess of the flux. The relative importance of the relativistic effects remain uncertain, depending on the abundances of various radioactive isotopes and other energy sources that may power the LC.

articleTitle: Relation between a Moreton Wave and an EIT Wave Observed on 1997 November 4
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We consider the relationship between two flare-associated waves, a chromospheric Moreton wave and a coronal EIT wave, based on an analysis of an X-class flare event in AR 8100 on 1997 November 4. A Moreton wave was observed in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm H}\alpha$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm H}\alpha {+} 0.8\,$</tex><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Å$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm H}\alpha-0.8\,$</tex><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Å$</tex> with the Flare-Monitoring Telescope (FMT) at the Hida Observatory. An EIT wave was observed in EUV with the Extreme ultraviolet Imaging Telescope (EIT) on board SOHO. The propagation speeds of the Moreton wave and the EIT wave were approximately <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$715 \,{\rm km} \,{\rm s}^{-1}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$202 \,{\rm km} \,{\rm s}^{-1}$</tex>, respectively. The times of visibility for the Moreton wave did not overlap those of the EIT wave, but the continuation of the former is indicated by a filament oscillation. Data on the speed and location clearly show that the Moreton wave differed physically from the EIT wave in this case. The Moreton wave preceded the EIT wave, which is inconsistent with an identification of the EIT wave with a fast-mode MHD shock.

articleTitle: Decomposition of the Superwind in M 82
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present new optical images (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B, V$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm{H}\alpha$</tex>) of the archetypical starburst/superwind galaxy M 82 obtained with the 8.2 m Subaru Telescope to reveal new detailed structures of the superwind-driven nebula and the high-latitude dark lanes. The emission-line nebula is decomposed into (1) a ridge-dominated component comprising numerous filament/loop sub-structures whose overall morphology appears as a pair of narrow cylinders, and (2) a diffuse component extended over much wider opening angle from the nucleus. We suggest that these two components have different origins. The ridge-dominated component appears as a pair of cylinders rather than a pair of cones. Since this morphological property is similar to that of hot plasma probed by soft X-ray, this component seems to surround the hot plasma. On the other hand, the diffuse component may arise from dust grains which scatter stellar light from the galaxy. Since inner region of this component is seen over the prominent “X”-shaped dark lanes streaming out from the nuclear region and they can be reproduced as a conical distribution of dust grains, there seems to be a dusty cold outflow as well as the hot one probed by soft X-ray and shock-excited optical emission lines. If this is the case, the presence of such high-latitude dust grains implies that neutral gaseous matter is also blown out during the course of the superwind activity.

articleTitle: Flat Spectrum X-Ray Emission from the Direction of a Molecular Cloud Associated with SNR RX J1713.7–3946
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report on the discovery of a diffuse X-ray source with ASCA, presumably associated with a molecular cloud in the vicinity of the supernova remnant RX J1713.7<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-$</tex>3946. The energy spectrum (1–10 keV) of the hard X-ray source shows a flat continuum, which is described by a power-law with a photon index of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma = 1.0^{+0.4}_{-0.3}$</tex>. We argue that this unusually flat spectrum can be best interpreted in terms of characteristic bremsstrahlung emission from the loss-flattened distribution of either sub-relativistic protons or mildly relativistic electrons. The strong shock of RX J1713.7<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-$</tex>3946, which is likely to interact with the molecular cloud, as evidenced by CO-line observations, seems to be a natural site of acceleration of such nonthermal particles. The observed luminosity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_{\rm X} = 1.7 \times 10^{35} \,{\rm erg} \,{\rm s}^{-1}$</tex> (for a distance of 6 kpc) seems to require a huge kinetic energy of about <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10^{50} \,{\rm erg}$</tex> in the form of nonthermal particles to illuminate the cloud. The shock-acceleration at RX J1713.7<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-$</tex>3946 can barely satisfy this energetic requirement, unless (i) the source is located much closer than the preferred distance of 6 kpc and/or (ii) the mechanical energy of the supernova explosion essentially exceeds <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10^{51} \,{\rm erg}$</tex>. Another possibility would be that an essential part of the lost energy due to the ionization and heating of gas, is somehow converted to plasma waves, which return this energy to nonthermal particles through their turbulent reacceleration on the plasma waves.

articleTitle: Abundances in Comet 19P/Borrelly at the Time of the Spacecraft Encounters
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: A spectroscopic observation of comet 19P/Borrelly was carried out on 2001 September 23, using a low-dispersion spectrograph in the wavelength range 3800–7600Å. It was performed about 20 hours after an encounter of the spacecraft Deep Space 1 (DS1) with the comet. We detected species such as CN, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm C}_2$</tex>, [O i], and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm NH}_2$</tex>, and estimated the gas-production rates of CN, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm C}_2$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm NH}_2$</tex> relative to that of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm H}_2{\rm O}$</tex> based on a Haser model. The production-rate ratios and the gas-to-dust ratio were: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q({\rm CN}) / Q({\rm H}_2{\rm O}) = 0.094\%$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q({\rm C}_2)/Q({\rm H}_2{\rm O}) = 0.096\%$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q({\rm NH}_2)/Q({\rm H}_2{\rm O}) = 0.13\%$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\log [Q({\rm H}_2{\rm O}) / Af\rho] = 26.0$</tex>. Our calculated relative production rates of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm C}_2$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm NH}_2$</tex> to CN were similar to those of previous apparitions. Therefore, the circumstances of the comet when DS1 encountered may be the same as those during the last several apparitions, and many ground-based observations performed during previous apparitions will be useful to reveal the nature of the comet during the in situ observations by DS1.

articleTitle: Subaru Prime Focus Camera — Suprime-Cam
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We have built an 80-mega pixels (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10240 \times 8192$</tex>) mosaic CCD camera, called Suprime-Cam, for the wide-field prime focus of the 8.2 m Subaru telescope. Suprime-Cam covers a field of view <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$34' \times 27'$</tex>, a unique facility among the 8–10 m class telescopes, with a resolution of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${0\rlap {.}{}^{\rm {\prime \prime }}202}$</tex> per pixel. The focal plane consists of ten high-resistivity <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\rm{k} \times 4\rm{k}$</tex> CCDs developed by MIT Lincoln Laboratory, which are cooled by a large Stirling-cycle cooler. The CCD readout electronics was designed to be scalable, which allows the multiple read-out of tens of CCDs. It takes 50 seconds to readout entire arrays. We designed a filter-exchange mechanism of the jukebox type that can hold up to ten large filters (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$205\times 170 \times 15 \,\rm{mm}^3$</tex>). The wide-field corrector is basically a three-lens Wynne-type, but has a new type of atmospheric dispersion corrector. The corrector provides a flat focal plane and an un-vignetted field of view of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$30'$</tex> in diameter. The achieved co-planarity of the focal array mosaic is smaller than 30<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\,{\mu \rm {m}}$</tex> peak-to-peak, which realizes mostly the seeing limited image over the entire field. The median seeing in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I_{\rm c}$</tex>-band, measured over one year and a half, is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${0\rlap {.}{}^{\rm {\prime \prime }}61}$</tex> . The PSF anisotropy in Suprime-Cam images, estimated by stellar ellipticities, is about 2% under this median seeing condition. At the time of commissioning, Suprime-Cam had the largest survey speed, which is defined as the field of view multiplied by the primary mirror area of the telescope, among those cameras built for sub-arcsecond imaging.

articleTitle: Absorption Line Survey of H3+ toward the Galactic Center Sources I. GCS 3-2 and GC IRS3
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present high-resolution (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R = 20000$</tex>) spectroscopy of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm{H}_3^{+}$</tex> absorption toward the luminous Galactic center sources GCS 3-2 and GC IRS 3. With the efficient wavelength coverage afforded by Subaru IRCS, six absorption lines of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm{H}_3^{+}$</tex> have been detected in each source from 3.5 to 4.0<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\, {\mu \rm {m}}$</tex>, three of which are new. In particular the 3.543<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\, {\mu \rm {m}}$</tex> absorption line of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R(3, 3)^l$</tex> transition arising from the metastable <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(J, K) = (3, 3)$</tex> state has been tentatively detected for the first time in the interstellar medium, where previous observations of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm{H}_3^{+}$</tex> had been limited to absorption lines from the lowest levels: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(J, K) = (1, 0)$</tex> of ortho-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm{H}_3^{+}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(1, 1)$</tex> of para-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm{H}_3^{+}$</tex>.The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm{H}_3^{+}$</tex> absorption toward the Galactic center takes place in dense and diffuse clouds along the line of sight as well as the molecular complex close to the Galactic nucleus. At least four kinematic components are found in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm{H}_3^{+}$</tex> absorption lines. We suggest identifications of the velocity components with those of H I, CO, and H<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_2$</tex>CO previously reported from radio and infrared observations. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm{H}_3^{+}$</tex> components with velocities that match those of weak and sharp CO and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm{H_{2}CO}$</tex> lines are attributed to diffuse clouds. Our observation has revealed a striking difference between the absorption profiles of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm{H}_3^{+}$</tex> and CO, demonstrating that the spectroscopy of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm{H}_3^{+}$</tex> provides information complementary to that obtained from CO spectroscopy.The tentative detection of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R(3, 3)^l$</tex> line and the non-detection of spectral lines from other <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J \gt 1$</tex> levels provide observational evidence for the metastability of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(3, 3)$</tex> level, which is theoretically expected. This suggests that other metastable <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J = K$</tex> levels with higher <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J$</tex> may also be populated.

articleTitle: Timing Observation of the Millisecond Pulsar PSR 1937 + 21 Using the Kashima 34 m-Antenna
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Communications Research Laboratory (CRL) has developed a precise measurement system for millisecond pulsar timing using the 34-m antenna at Kashima Space Research Center, one of the smallest antennas for millisecond pulsar observations. Timing observations of the millisecond pulsar PSR 1937 + 21 have been ongoing since 1997 November at Kashima. From observational data of almost three years, we obtained a timing accuracy of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.65 \,\mu{\rm s}$</tex> from daily-averaged residuals, and found the frequency stability to be about <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1 \times 10^{-13}$</tex> over a period of one year. This result confirms the observational sensitivity of our system, and shows the possibility of constructing a pulsar time scale by using a system with a small antenna.

articleTitle: Statistical Method for Deriving Spatial and Size Distributions of Sub-km Main-Belt Asteroids from Their Sky Motions
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: The importance of sub-kilometer-sized objects among the main-belt asteroids (MBAs) has been progressively recognized in relation to the origin of near-Earth asteroids and the formation of rubble-pile asteroids. However, exact orbit determinations of those individual objects are practically impossible, because both their discovery and subsequent follow-up observations require 8–10 m class telescopes, in which observation-time competition is severe. Therefore, we examine here instead a statistical method to deduce the spatial and size distributions of sub-km MBAs from only their apparent motion vectors on the sky. Assuming their near-opposition and near-ecliptic observations, we made simulations to estimate the accuracy of the semi-major axis (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a$</tex>) and inclination (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I$</tex>) obtained from their sky-motion vectors. The mean errors of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I$</tex> for each asteroid were found to be about 0.15 AU and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1^\circ \hbox{-} 2^\circ$</tex> (for the asteroids with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I < 10^\circ$</tex>), respectively. Then, under a certain assumption, we calculated magnitudes and the size distribution of those computer-synthesized sub-km MBAs. Our statistical method could reproduce the slope of the cumulative size distribution for the original asteroid populations with errors of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim0.05 \hbox{-} 0.1$</tex>. These values are small enough for our survey purposes using the Subaru Telescope.

articleTitle: Subaru/HDS Study of the Extremely Metal-Poor Star CS 29498-043: Abundance Analysis Details and Comparison with Other Carbon-Rich Objects
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report on the details of an abundance study using the Subaru Telescope High Dispersion Spectrograph for the extremely metal-poor (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$[\rm{Fe/H}] =-3.75$</tex>) star CS 29498-043, whose overabundances of C, N, Mg, and Si were reported in our previous work. The effect of the large overabundance of Mg found in this object on the stellar atmosphere is included in the abundance analysis. We also performed a similar analysis for the other eight carbon-rich, metal-poor (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-2.7 < [{\rm Fe/H}] <-1.9$</tex>) stars with excesses of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s$</tex>-process elements, and for the carbon-rich object CS 22957-027 which shows no excess of neutron-capture elements. Neutron-capture elements in CS 29498-043, as well as CS 22949-037 which is also known to have large excesses of C, N, Mg, and Si, do not show any overabundance. This fact clearly distinguishes these two stars from other carbon-rich objects with excesses of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s$</tex>-process elements. The abundances of Mg, Al, and Si in CS 29498-043 and CS 22949-037 are significantly higher than those in other carbon-rich objects and non-carbon-rich stars with similar metallicities. The abundance nature of these two stars suggests the existence of a class of extremely metal-poor stars with large excesses of C, N, Mg, Al, and Si, which presumably originate from supernovae in which relatively little material escaped from the iron core.

articleTitle: The Multiwavelength Doppler Factors for a Sample of Gamma-Ray Loud Blazars
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: The high luminosity and rapid variability detected in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma$</tex>-ray loud blazars imply that the beaming effect plays an important role in these sources. The Doppler factor, depending on two unobservable parameters (Lorentz factor and viewing angle), is very important for understanding the basic properties of blazars. Although the viewing angle is unobservable, increasing direct and indirect evidence has shown up to indicate that the jet is bent, and therefore the viewing angle also varies. In this sense, the Doppler factor, which is dependent on the viewing angle and the Lorentz factor, should also vary. In the present paper, using available data of blazars at different (radio, optical, X-ray, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma$</tex>-ray) wavebands and assuming that multi-waveband radiation is produced by the radiation of accelerated particles in a jet, we discuss the properties of the Doppler factors of blazars at different wavebands. Our results indicate that the Doppler factor of a blazar is a function of frequency. The Doppler factor decreases with frequency from radio to X-ray bands, but increases with frequency from X-ray to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma$</tex>-ray bands. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma$</tex>-ray Doppler factors found in the present paper are correlated with those by Ghisellini et al. (1998, AAA070.159.155), suggesting that our estimation is reasonable. Furthermore, BL Lacertae objects are found to show lower Doppler factors and higher synchrotron peak frequencies compared with FSRQs; the promising TeV sources are BL Lacertae objects.

articleTitle: Composite Luminosity Functions Based on the Sloan Digital Sky Survey “Cut and Enhance” Galaxy Cluster Catalog
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present here results on the composite luminosity functions (LF) of galaxies in the clusters of galaxies selected from the Cut and Enhance cluster catalog (CE) of the Sloan Digital Sky Survey. We constructed composite LFs in the five SDSS bands, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u, g, r, i$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z$</tex>, using 204 CE clusters ranging from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z = 0.02$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z = 0.25$</tex> . Background and foreground galaxies were subtracted from the LF using an annular region around clusters to take large-scale, galaxy-number-count variances into consideration. A LF of each cluster was weighted according to the richness and number of contributing galaxies to construct the composite LF. Taking advantage of accurate photometry of SDSS, we used photometric redshifts to construct composite luminosity functions and thus study a large number of clusters. The robustness of the weighting scheme was tested using a Monte-Carlo simulation. The best-fit Schechter parameters are <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(M^*, \alpha) = (-21.61 \pm 0.26,-1.40 \pm0.11), (-22.01 \pm 0.11,-1.00 \pm 0.06), (-22.21 \pm 0.05,-0.85 \pm 0.03), (-22.31 \pm 0.08,-0.70 \pm 0.05)$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(-21.36 \pm 0.06,-0.58 \pm 0.04)$</tex> in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u, g, r, i$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z$</tex>, respectively. We find that the slope of composite LFs becomes flatter toward a redder color band. Compared with the field LFs of the SDSS, the cluster LFs have brighter characteristic magnitude and flatter slopes in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g, r, i$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z$</tex> bands. These results are consistent with the hypothesis that the cluster LF has two distinct underlying populations; i.e. the bright end of the LF is dominated by bright early types that follow a Gaussian-like luminosity distribution, while the faint-end of the cluster LF is a steep power-law like function dominated by star-forming (bluer) galaxies. We also studied the composite LFs for early-type and late-type galaxies using profile fits, a concentration parameter and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u-r$</tex> color to classify galaxy morphology. A strong dependence of LF on galaxy morphology was found. The faint end slope of the LF is always flatter for early-type galaxies than late-type, regardless of the passband and methodology. These results are consistent with the hypothesis that the cluster regions are dominated by bright elliptical galaxies. This work also provides a good low-redshift benchmark for on-going multi-color photometric studies of high redshift clusters of galaxies using 4–8m class telescopes.

articleTitle: Time-Resolved Photometry of GK Persei during the 1996 Outburst
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: GK Per is a unique cataclysmic variable star which has shown a nova explosion as well as dwarf nova-type outbursts, and has an intermediate-polar nature. We carried out <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex>-band time-resolved photometry and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B$</tex>-band monitoring during the 1996 outburst. This outburst lasted for about 60 d, and was divided into three parts: a slow-rise branch for 35 d, a gradual-decay branch with a decay rate of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$20.0 \,{\rm d} \,{\rm mag}^{-1}$</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 16 \,{\rm d}$</tex>, and a rapid-decline branch with a rate of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5.6 \,{\rm d} \,{\rm mag}^{-1}$</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 10 \,{\rm d}$</tex>. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B-V$</tex> color became bluest (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B-V \sim 0.18$</tex>) at about 10 d before the outburst maximum, which supports an idea that the outburst in GK Per is of the inside-out type. The spin pulse, 440-s quasi periodic oscillations (QPOs), and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 5000$</tex>-s QPOs were detected in our light curve, as previously seen in X-ray and optical observations. In addition, we report on the discovery of an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 300$</tex>-s periodicity, which is shorter than the spin period.

articleTitle: Observations of Ammonia in External Galaxies I. NGC 253 and M 82
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: The ammonia <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(J,K) = (1,1)$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(2,2)$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(3,3)$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(4,4)$</tex> transitions in the 23.7–24.1 GHz region were searched for in nearby galaxies, NGC 253 and M 82, to study the relation between the molecular abundances and physical conditions. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(1,1)$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(2,2)$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(3,3)$</tex> emission lines were clearly detected in NGC 253, but no lines were found in M 82. In NGC 253 the shapes of the three emission lines were different from one another. The rotational temperatures obtained in NGC 253 were <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lesssim 17 \hbox{-} 50 \,{\rm K}$</tex>, depending on the velocity components. There are two main results: (1) The ortho-to-para abundance ratio was obtained in NGC 253 and found to be different depending on the velocity components. The ratio was about 1 for the velocity component where the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(2,2)$</tex> line is detected. On the other hand, the ratio was more than 6 for another velocity component where the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(2,2)$</tex> line is barely detected. This high ratio corresponds to an equilibration temperature of less than 8 K between ortho and para. (2) The abundance of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm NH}_3$</tex> in NGC 253 was found to be about an order of magnitude larger than the upper limit in M 82. This result is an additional evidence for the different molecular abundances which were already reported between NGC 253 and M 82. In addition, the molecular abundances including <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm NH}_3$</tex> in nearby galaxies with rich molecular gas were compared, and we found that the molecular abundance in M 82 is systematically peculiar concerning the formation mechanisms of molecules. We discussed factors which cause such a peculiarity in M 82.

articleTitle: Study of the X-Ray Background Spectrum and Its Large-Scale Fluctuation with ASCA
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We studied the energy spectrum and the large-scale fluctuation of the X-ray background with the ASCA GIS instrument based on the ASCA Medium Sensitivity Survey and Large Sky Survey observations. A total of 91 fields with Galactic latitude <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$|b| \gt 10^\circ$</tex> were selected with a sky coverage of 50 deg<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^2$</tex> and 4.2 Ms of exposure. For each field, non-X-ray events were carefully subtracted and sources brighter than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 2\times 10^{-13} \,\rm{erg} \,\rm{cm}^{-2} \,\rm{s}^{-1}$</tex> (2–10 keV) were eliminated. Spectral fits with a single power-law model for the individual 0.7–10 keV spectra showed a significant excess below <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 2 \,\rm{keV}$</tex>, which could be expressed by an additional thermal model with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$kT\simeq 0.4 \,\rm{keV}$</tex> or a steep power-law model with a photon index of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma^{\rm soft}\simeq 6$</tex>. The 0.5–2 keV intensities of the soft thermal component varied significantly from field to field by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1\,\sigma= 52^{+4}_{-5}\%$</tex>, and showed a maximum toward the Galactic Center. This component is considered to be entirely Galactic. As for the hard power-law component, an average photon index of 91 fields was obtained to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma^{\rm hard} = 1.412 \pm 0.007 \pm 0.025$</tex> and the average 2–10 keV intensity was calculated as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F_{\rm X}^{\rm hard} = (6.38 \pm 0.04 \pm 0.64) \times 10^{-8}\,{\rm erg} \,{\rm cm}^{-2} \,{\rm s}^{-1} \,{\rm sr}^{-1}$</tex> (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1\,\sigma$</tex> statistical and systematic errors). The Galactic component is marginally detected in the hard band. The 2–10 keV intensities show a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1\,\sigma$</tex> deviation of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$6.49^{+0.56}_{-0.61}\%$</tex>, while deviation due to the reproducibility of the particle background is 3.2%. The observed deviation can be explained by the Poisson noise of the source count in the f.o.v. (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 0.5 \,\rm{deg}^2$</tex>), even assuming a single <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\log{N} \hbox{-} \log{S}$</tex> relation on the whole sky. Based on the observed fluctuation and the absolute intensity, an acceptable region of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\log{N} \hbox{-} \log{S}$</tex> relation was derived, showing a consistent feature with the recent Chandra and XMM-Newton results. The fluctuation of the spectral index was also examined; it implied a large amount of hard sources and a substantial variation in the intrinsic source spectra (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma_{\rm S} \simeq 1.1 \pm 1.0$</tex>).

articleTitle: Spectroscopic Determination of Stellar Atmospheric Parameters: Application to Mid-F through Early-K Dwarfs and Subgiants
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Takeda et al.–s (, PASJ, 54, 451) method for the spectroscopic determination of stellar atmospheric parameters (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_{\rm eff}, \log g, v_{\rm t}$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$[{\rm Fe/H}]$</tex>) from the equivalent widths of Fe I and Fe II lines was applied to 32 dwarfs/subgiants of mid-F through early-K types based on high-quality echelle spectra obtained at Okayama Astrophysical Observatory, for the purpose of examining the numerical performance of this technique as well as the precision of the results. The solutions of the parameters were confirmed to successfully converge, except for a few cases (e.g., for lower temperature and lower metallicity stars) where the microturbulent velocity could not be well determined. A comparison of the present results with the literature values, especially those of Fuhrmann (, AAA070.155.024), revealed that the agreement is mostly satisfactory, though a systematic tendency appears to exist that our method yields slightly lower (i.e., by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 100 \,{\rm K}$</tex>) <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_{\rm eff}$</tex> values. The results are further discussed in relation to the stellar fundamental parameters (mass, luminosity, etc.), while referring to the Hipparcos parallaxes or theoretical stellar evolutionary tracks.

articleTitle: Super-Eddington Black-Hole Models for SS 433
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We examine highly super-Eddington black-hole models for SS 433, based on two-dimensional hydrodynamical calculations coupled with radiation transport. The super-Eddington accretion flow with a small viscosity parameter, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha = 10^{-3}$</tex>, results in a geometrically–and optically-thick disk with a large opening angle of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 60^{\circ}$</tex> to the equatorial plane and a very rarefied, hot, and optically-thin high-velocity jets region around the disk. The thick accretion flow consists of two different zones: an inner advection-dominated zone and an outer convection-dominated zone. The high-velocity region around the disk is divided into two characteristic regions, a very rarefied funnel region along the rotational axis and a moderately rarefied high-velocity region outside of the disk. The temperatures of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 10^7 \,{\rm K}$</tex> and the densities of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 10^{-7} \,{\rm g} \,{\rm cm}^{-3}$</tex> in the upper disk vary sharply to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 10^8 \,{\rm K}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10^{-8}\,{\rm g} \,{\rm cm}^{-3}$</tex>, respectively, across the disk boundary between the disk and the high-velocity region. The X-ray emission of iron lines would be generated only in a confined region between the funnel wall and the photospheric disk boundary, where flows are accelerated to relativistic velocities of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 0.2 \,c$</tex> due to the dominant radiation-pressure force. The results are discussed regarding the collimation angle of the jets, the large mass-outflow rate observed in SS 433, and the ADAFs and the CDAFs models.

articleTitle: Collisional Evolution of Galaxy Clusters and the Growth of Common Halos
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We investigated the dynamical evolution of clusters of galaxies in virial equilibrium using Fokker–Planck models and self-consistent <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex>-body models. In particular, we focused on the growth of a common halo, which is a cluster-wide halo formed by matter stripped from galaxies, and the development of a central density cusp. The Fokker–Planck models include the effects of two-body gravitational encounters both between galaxies and between galaxies and common halo particles. The effects of tidal mass stripping from the galaxies due to close galaxy–galaxy encounters and accompanying dissipation of the orbital kinetic energies of the galaxies were also taken into account in the Fokker–Planck models. We find that the results of the Fokker–Planck models are in excellent agreement with those of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex>-body models regarding the growth of the common halo mass and the evolution of the cluster density profiles. In the central region of the cluster, a shallow density cusp, approximated by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rho (r) \propto r^{-\alpha}$</tex> (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha \sim 1$</tex>), develops. This shallow cusp results from the combined effects of two-body relaxation and tidal stripping. The cusp steepness, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex>, weakly depends on the relative importance of the tidal stripping. When the effect of stripping is important, the central velocity dispersion decreases as the central density increases and, consequently, a shallow (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha <2$</tex>) cusp is formed. In the limit of no stripping, usual gravothermal core collapse occurs, i.e. the central velocity dispersion increases as the central density increases with a steep (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha \gt 2$</tex>) cusp left. We conclude from our consideration of the origin of the cusp demonstrated here that shallow cusps should develop in real galaxy clusters.

articleTitle: Chandra Observations and Optical Identification of Hard X-Ray Sources Discovered with ASCA
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present the first results of Chandra and optical follow-up observations of hard X-ray sources detected in the ASCA Medium Sensitivity Survey (AMSS). Optical identifications were made for five objects. Three of them show either weak or absent optical narrow emission lines, and are at low redshift <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\langle z \rangle \sim 0.06$</tex>. One of them is a broad line object at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z = 0.910$</tex> and one is a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z = 0.460$</tex> object with only narrow lines. All of the narrow-line objects show strong evidence of absorption in their X-ray spectra. Their line ratios are consistent with a Seyfert II/LINER identification, as are the line widths. The three low-redshift objects have the colors of normal galaxies, and apparently the light is dominated by stars. This could be due to extinction of the underlying nuclear continuum by the same matter that absorbs X-rays and/or due to dilution of the central source by starlight. These results suggest that X-ray sources that appear as “normal” galaxies in optical and near-IR bands significantly contribute to the hard X-ray background. This population of objects has a high space density, and probably dominates the entire population of active galaxies.

articleTitle: Energy Spectra and Normalized Power Spectral Densities of X-Ray Nova GS 2000+25
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: The X-ray energy spectra and Normalized Power Spectral Densities (NPSDs) of an X-ray nova, GS 2000<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+$</tex>25, were investigated. The X-ray energy spectra of the source consist of two components: a hard component, which can be represented by a power-law, and an ultra-soft component, represented by radiation from an optically-thick accretion disk (the disk component). In a model in which the power-law component is the Compton-scattered radiation, it is found that the temperature of the incident blackbody radiation to the Compton cloud decreases from 0.8 keV to 0.2 keV according to the decay of the intensity, which coincides with that of the inner accretion disk. When the source changed from the high-state to the low-state, both the photon index of the power-law component (or Compton <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$y$</tex>-parameter) and the NPSD of the hard component dramatically changed as did GS 1124<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-$</tex>683. That is, the photon index changed from 2.2–2.6 to 1.7–1.8 and the absolute values of the NPSDs at 0.3 Hz of the hard component in the low-state became about 10-times larger than those of the hard component in the high-state. These X-ray properties were similar to those of other black-hole candidates, such as Cyg X-1, GX 339-4, and LMC X-3.

articleTitle: Lagrangian Statistical Theory of Anisotropic MHD Turbulence
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We construct a Lagrangian statistical theory of spatially uniform, anisotropic, and strong turbulence of an incompressible magneto-fluid with a uniform mean magnetic field. We treat shear Alfvén turbulence; that is, the perturbations of the velocity field and the magnetic field are assumed to be orthogonal to the mean magnetic field. The perturbation energies, however, need not be equiparted; our theory covers non-equipartition turbulence as well as equipartition turbulence. We show that, concerning the relaxation and energy-transfer of inertial-range eddies, the shear Alfvén turbulence has the following fundamental properties: That is, relaxation of inertial-range eddies is dominated by the largest (energy-containing) eddies; energy cascades have spatially a quasi 2-dimensional nature because of the inhibition of cascades parallel to the mean field; thus, inevitably, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-3/2$</tex> power-law energy-spectra are derived. These properties are independent of whether the turbulence satisfies the energy equipartition. We, therefore, assert that they should be thought of as generic and robust natures of strong MHD turbulence.

articleTitle: On the Abundance of Potassium in Metal-Poor Stars
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Based on extensive statistical-equilibrium calculations, we performed a non-LTE analysis of the K i 7699 equivalent-width data of metal-deficient stars for the purpose of clarifying the behavior of the photospheric potassium abundance in disk/halo stars. While the resulting non-LTE abundance corrections turned out to be considerably large, amounting to 0.2–0.7 dex, their effect on the [K/Fe] vs. [Fe/H] relation is not very important, since these corrections do not show any significant dependence on the metallicity. Hence, we again confirmed the results of previous LTE studies, that [K/Fe] shows a gradual systematic increase toward a lowered metallicity up to [K/Fe] <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$sim$</tex> 0.3–0.5 at [Fe/H] <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$sim$</tex><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-</tex>1 to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-</tex>2, such as in the case of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> elements.

articleTitle: Disk–Halo Model for Flat-Spectrum T Tauri Stars
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We explore the origin of the flat spectrum seen in some T Tauri stars by considering a three-component structure: a central star, a circumstellar disk, and a dusty halo. The radiative energy transport is faithfully treated by solving the angle- and frequency-dependent radiative transfer equation in two space dimensions assuming axisymmetry, and hence the radiative equilibrium temperature in the disk and halo is determined simultaneously. The disk is effectively heated by the scattering and reprocessing of stellar radiation through the halo. The large mid- to far-infrared excess originates from the photosphere of the warmed disk, resulting in a flat spectrum, as observed. The halo which we consider is observed as a compact reflection nebula, and is discriminated from extended, disk-like envelopes around flat-spectrum T Tauri stars. We show that the overall spectral shape of flat-spectrum T Tauri stars can be reproduced by the present disk–halo model.

articleTitle: Three-Dimensional Genus Statistics of Galaxies in the SDSS Early Data Release
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present the first analysis of three-dimensional genus statistics for the SDSS EDR galaxy sample. Due to the complicated survey volume and the selection function, analytic predictions of the genus statistics for this sample are not feasible; therefore, we construct extensive mock catalogs from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex>-body simulations in order to compare the observed data with model predictions. This comparison allows us to evaluate the effects of a variety of observational systematics on the estimated genus for the SDSS sample, including the shape of the survey volume, the redshift distortion effect, and the radial selection function due to the magnitude limit. The observed genus for the SDSS EDR galaxy sample is consistent with that predicted by simulations of a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Lambda$</tex>-dominated spatially-flat cold dark matter model. Standard (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega_0=1$</tex>) cold dark matter model predictions do not match the observations. We discuss how future SDSS galaxy samples will yield improved estimates of the genus.

articleTitle: Origin of the “Disk-Line” Feature in the X-Ray Energy Spectrum of a Seyfert Galaxy, NGC 4151
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We have studied the origin of the broad and skewed feature at 4.5–7.5 keV in the energy spectra of NGC 4151 using the ASCA and RXTE data. The feature consists of a narrow peak at 6.4 keV and a broad wing extended between 4.5–7.5 keV. An analysis of the long-term variations revealed that the feature became variable only on a time scale longer than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.5 \times 10^6 \,\rm{s}$</tex>. Through a comparison with the continuum variabilities, we found that the emission region of the excess flux at 4.5–7.5 keV has an extent of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10^{17} \,\rm{cm}$</tex>. The broad and skewed feature at 4.5–7.5 keV may be explained by the so-called “disk-line” model. If so, the size of the line-emitting region, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10^{17} \,\rm{cm}$</tex>, should be equal to several or ten times the Schwarzschild radius of the central black hole. This results in a black hole mass of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10^{11} \,{{{M}_{\odot}}}$</tex>, which may be too large for NGC 4151. We propose an alternative explanation for the broad and skewed feature, i.e. a “reflection” model, which can also reproduce the overall energy spectra very well.
