In this model, cold matter with a sufficiently large column density is irradiated by X-rays to produce a reflected continuum, which constitutes the broad wing of the feature and narrow fluorescent lines. The equivalent width of the iron fluorescent line (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 2 \,\rm{keV}$</tex>) and the upper limit of its width (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma < 92 \,{\rm eV}$</tex>) are also consistent with this model. From these results and considerations, we conclude that the “disk-line” model has difficulty to explain the spectral variations of NGC 4151, and the reflection model is more plausible.

articleTitle: Tridimensional Spectroscopic Observation of the Interacting System NGC 7592
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We performed a tridimensional spectroscopic study of NGC 7592, an infrared-luminous interacting system of three galaxies, one of which contains a Seyfert 2 nucleus. Narrow-band images of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm{H}\alpha$</tex> and [O iii] were obtained using an imaging Fabry–Perot interferometer with a tunable filter. An area-spectroscopic observation was also made by a slit scan in a direction perpendicular to the slit. The Seyfert nucleus was found to be surrounded by a knotty star-forming region of disk- or ring-shape. Along the axis of the disk or ring, a highly-ionized bipolar gaseous region was identified. From kinematical analyses, it has been suggested that this system is composed of two galaxies; one apparent nucleus is considered to be a giant H ii region belonging to one galaxy. This result is supported by the morphological properties in near-infrared. Further, it has been suggested that one galaxy is an early-type spiral, whereas the other is a late-type one, and the two galaxies show a marked difference in the distribution of the star-forming regions within each. The cause of the difference was argued in relation with the dynamical perturbation between the two galaxies.

articleTitle: Spectroscopic Determination of Atmospheric Parameters of Solar-Type Stars: Description of the Method and Application to the Sun
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: A computer program has been developed for determining the fundamental model atmosphere parameters (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_{\rm eff}$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\log g$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v_{\rm t}$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$[{\rm Fe/H}]$</tex>) of solar-type stars, which is based on the equivalent widths for a well-chosen set of Fe i and Fe ii lines. The basic principle of this method is to find the solution in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(T_{\rm eff}$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\log g$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v_{\rm t})$</tex> space, which minimizes the sum of the dispersion of the Fe i abundances and the square of the Fe i–Fe ii abundance difference. An application of this code to the observed solar equivalent widths turned out to yield satisfactory results, which are more or less consistent with the actual parameters of the Sun. The numerical performance of this approach as well as the errors involved in the resulting solutions are discussed.

articleTitle: Radiative–Thermal Winds from an Accretion Disk
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We examine a hydrodynamical wind, which emanates from an accretion disk and is driven by thermal and radiation pressures, under a one-dimensional approximation along supposed streamlines. Such a disk wind is characterized by the disk gravitational and radiation fields, whose behavior is rather different from the spherical case. Along the streamline of winds, the gravitational field produced by the central object generally has a peak at some height, unlike the spherical case where it decreases monotonically. The radiation field produced by the disk, on the other hand, is almost constant near to the disk surface and decreases far from the disk, again unlike the spherical case. Due to these characteristic properties of force fields, disk winds are classified into three patterns: in the cold less-luminous case no wind can blow, in the warm luminous case transonic winds are established, and beyond some critical luminosity disk winds are always supersonic. We found that transonic winds can blow for the parameter range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a_0 + 2\Gamma_{\rm eff} \gtrsim 0.8$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a_0$</tex> is the initial sound speed in units of the Keplerian speed at the wind base and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma_{\rm eff}$</tex> the normalized disk luminosity at the wind base. Furthermore, supersonic winds blow for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma_{\rm eff} \gtrsim 0.4$</tex>. We derive the terminal speed as a function of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma_{\rm eff}$</tex>. A radial extension of the flow is also discussed and applied to mass outflow from several active objects.

articleTitle: Orbital Stability of a Protoplanet System under a Drag Force Proportional to the Random Velocity
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We investigated the effects of a tidal interaction with a gas disk and the dynamical friction with a planetesimal disk on the orbital instability of a protoplanet system. Both effects are expressed as the drag force, which is proportional to the random velocity of a protoplanet. We calculated numerically the orbits of 5 protoplanets with the same separation distance under the drag-force effect and examined the orbital instability time under the drag force, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_{{\rm inst}}^{{\rm df}}$</tex>. We found that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_{{\rm inst}}^{{\rm df}}$</tex> can become much larger than the instability time under the drag-free condition, and that the onset of the orbital instability is prevented when the separation distance exceeds a critical value. We obtained a relation between the critical separation distance and the surface density of the gas or planetesimal disk. By applying this relation, we found that, for the formation of terrestrial planets from a protoplanet system with a typical orbital separation (i.e., <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 10$</tex> Hill radii), the surface density of the nebular gas must be reduced to about one-thousandth of that in the minimum-mass nebula model. Terrestrial planets would be formed after such a depletion of the solar nebula.

articleTitle: α Element Abundances in Mildly Metal-Poor Stars
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present [O/Fe] and other <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex>-elements/Fe ratios in a sample of 24 mildly metal-poor stars. The sample stars are thought to be brighter than 9.0 magnitude and have available <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u\upsilon{by}$</tex> photometric data. Also, based on the typical LTE abundance analysis, we find that [Si/Fe] and [Ca/Fe] are correlated with each other. Combining the kinematic data and the metallicity, we can classify the sample stars into three groups. An abundance analysis shows some evidence that these groups are chemically discrete from each other. Further, the general trend of a decreasing overabundance of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> elements with increasing metallicity has been confirmed.

articleTitle: Development of Iodine Cells for the Subaru HDS and the Okayama HIDES: I. Instrumentation and Performance of the Spectrographs
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We have developed iodine (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm{I}_2$</tex>) cells for the High Dispersion Spectrograph (HDS) on the Subaru telescope and for the HIgh Dispersion Echelle Spectrograph (HIDES) on the Okayama 1.88m reflector. The cell is put into a compact vacuum vessel, which fits into a small space behind the entrance slit of the HDS. The cell assembly is designed to minimize heat losses from the cell, which is heated during observations, to keep <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm{I}_2$</tex> vapor from condensation. The amount of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm{I}_2$</tex> in the cell is determined to be best suited for radial-velocity measurements of solar-type stars. We also report on some performances of the HDS and HIDES as well as their instrumental profiles based on tests of our <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm{I}_2$</tex> cells. Lastly, we discuss future improvements of our instruments and data-analysis softwares for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm{I}_2$</tex> observations, and also describe the scientific goals of our project.

articleTitle: Short-Period Noncontact Close Binary Systems. VI. V392 Orionis
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Photometric and spectroscopic observations in the optical region of the short-period eclipsing binary system V392 Ori (A5 V, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P = 0.6593 \,\rm{d}$</tex>) were performed and light and radial velocity curves were obtained. The light curves taken at various times are slightly different from one another. Analyses of the light and radial velocity curves yielded photometric and spectroscopic elements of the system. The derived mass function is quite small, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f(M) = 0.0108 \,{{{M}_{\odot}}}$</tex>. The masses of the primary and secondary components were found to be 1.2<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${M}_{\odot}$</tex> and 0.3<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${M}_{\odot}$</tex>, respectively, and the radii are 1.7<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${R}_{\odot}$</tex> and 0.9<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${R}_{\odot}$</tex>. V392 Ori was found to belong to a group of low-mass binary systems. Due to the semidetached nature of the system, the loss of mass/angular momentum from the system may occasionally occur, inducing a probable effect on the light curves of the system. We compare the system with other low-mass binary systems and discuss the evolutionary status of the system.

articleTitle: Abundance Analyses of 12 Parent Stars of Extrasolar Planets Observed with the SUBARU/HDS
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: High <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm{S/N}$</tex> ratio (350–600) and high resolution (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R \sim 90000$</tex>) spectral data covering the wavelength region between 4200–8800, Å were obtained for 12 planet-harboring stars with the SUBARU/HDS. Detailed abundance analyses were carried out for these stars using the solar spectrum as a reference. Atmospheric parameters (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_{\rm eff}, \log g$</tex>, microturbulent velocity <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\xi_{\rm t}$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$[{\rm Fe/H}]$</tex>) were determined spectroscopically using selected Fe I and Fe II lines. The abundances of 25 other elements have been determined relative to the Sun in a strictly differential manner. Three out of 12 stars (HD 82943, HD 92788, and HD 134987) are definitely metal rich, and two stars (HD 114762 and HD 190228) are metal deficient. The abundances in the remaining seven stars (HD 106252, HD 130322, HD 141937, HD 168746, HD 187123, HD 192263, HD 209458) coincide with the Sun. We find that the abundances of both volatile and refractory elements behave similarly in these stars, and do not confirm any significant dependence on the condensation temperature, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_{\rm c}$</tex>. Comparisons of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$[\rm{X/Fe}]$</tex> vs <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$[\rm{Fe/H}]$</tex> relations for 19 elements between planet-harboring stars and nearby field stars reveal no distinct anomaly, except for possible enhancements of V and Co in the former group. These results suggest that the observed over-abundances of metallic elements in planet-harboring stars relative to normal disk stars in the solar neighborhood are primordial, and can be interpreted as being a consequence of the galactic chemical evolution.

articleTitle: Variation of Molecular Cloud Properties across the Spiral Arm in M 51
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present the results of high-resolution <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{13\atop} {\rm CO}}$</tex> (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J = 1 \hbox{-} 0$</tex>) mapping observations with the NRO 45m telescope of the area toward the southern bright arm region of M 51, including the galactic center, in order to study the physical conditions of the molecular clouds in the arm and the interarm. The obtained map shows the central depression of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{13\atop} {\rm CO}}$</tex> (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J = 1 \hbox{-} 0$</tex>) emission, the circumnuclear ring (radius <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${10{}^{\mathrm {\prime \prime }}}$</tex>–<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${20{}^{\rm {\prime \prime }}}$</tex>), and the spiral arm structure. The arm-to-interarm ratio of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{13\atop} {\rm CO}}$</tex> (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J = 1 \hbox{-} 0$</tex>) integrated intensity is 2–4. We also have found a feature different from that found in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{12\atop} {\rm CO}}$</tex> results. For example, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{13\atop} {\rm CO}}$</tex> distribution shows a depression in part of the spiral arm. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{12\atop} {\rm CO}}/{{13\atop} {\rm CO}}$</tex> ratio spatially varies, and shows high values (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 20$</tex>) for the interarm and the central region, but low values (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 10$</tex>) for the arm. Their values indicate that there is a denser gas in the spiral arm than in the interarm.The distribution of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{13\atop} {\rm CO}}$</tex> shows a better correspondence with that of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm H}\alpha$</tex> emission than with the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{12\atop} {\rm CO}}$</tex> in the disk region, except for the central region. We found that the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{13\atop} {\rm CO}}$</tex> emission is located on the downstream side of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{12\atop} {\rm CO}}$</tex> arm, namely there is an offset between the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{12\atop} {\rm CO}}$</tex> and the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{13\atop} {\rm CO}}$</tex> as well as the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm H}\alpha$</tex> emission. This suggests that there is a time delay between the accumulation of gas caused by the density wave and dense gas formation, accordingly star formation. This time delay is estimated to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 10^7 \,{\rm yr}$</tex> based on the assumption of galactic rotation derived by the rotation curve and the pattern speed of the M 51 spiral pattern. It is similar to the growth timescale of a gravitational instability in the spiral arm of M 51, suggesting that the gravitational instability plays an important role for dense gas formation.

articleTitle: WZ Sge-Type Star V592 Herculis
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We observed the entire course of the 1998 outburst of V592 Her, which was originally reported as a nova in 1968. We have been able to construct a full light curve of the outburst, which is characterized by a rapid initial decline (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.98 \,\rm{mag} \,\rm{d}^{-1}$</tex>), which smoothly developed into a plateau phase with a slower linear decline. We detected superhumps characteristic to SU UMa-type dwarf novae <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 7 \,\rm{d}$</tex> after the optical maximum. The overall behavior of the light curve and the development of superhumps were characteristic to a WZ Sge-type dwarf nova. Combined with the past literature, we have been able to uniquely determine the superhump period to be 0.05648(2) d. From this period, together with a modern interpretation of the absolute magnitude of the outburst light curve, we conclude that the overall picture of V592 Her is not inconsistent with a lower main-sequence secondary star, in contrast to a previous claim that V592 Her contains a brown dwarf.

articleTitle: Radial Distributions of the HCN/CO Ratio in Nearby CO Bright Galaxies
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Simultaneous observations of HCN and CO lines were made along the major axes of six nearby CO bright galaxies with the Nobeyama 45-m telescope. The beam-averaged HCN/CO ratios are 0.01 to 0.1. The distributions of the HCN/CO ratio along the major axes (and the minor axis for M 51) show different patterns from one galaxy to another. By adding data obtained from the outer disk, however, we found gradual decreases in the HCN and CO intensities and the HCN/CO ratio with increasing radius in M 51 from the nuclear region to 3 kpc, similar to our previous result for NGC 253. The HCN/CO ratio is very sensitive to the observing beam size on a linear scale. The ratio, which reflects the fraction of dense molecular gas, correlates with the star-formation activity derived from the far-infrared luminosity.

Author Keywords: galaxies: individual (Maffei 2, IC 342, NGC 2146, M 82, M 51, NGC 6946)

articleTitle: Diffuse and Gravitationally Stable Molecular Gas in the Post-Starburst Galaxy NGC 5195
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: The Nobeyama Millimeter Array (NMA) has been used to make aperture synthesis CO(<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1-0$</tex>) observations of the post-starburst galaxy NGC 5195. CO(<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1-0$</tex>) and HCN(<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1-0$</tex>) observations of NGC 5195 using the Nobeyama 45 m telescope are also presented. High-resolution (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${1\rlap {.}{}^{\rm {\prime \prime }}9} \times {1\rlap {.}{}^{\rm {\prime \prime }}8}$</tex> or <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$86 \,\rm{pc} \times 81 \,\rm{pc}$</tex> resolution at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D = 9.3 \,\rm{Mpc}$</tex>) NMA maps show a strong concentration of CO emission toward the central a few <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times 100 \,\rm{pc}$</tex> region of NGC 5195, despite the fact that the current massive star formation is suppressed there. The face-on gas surface density, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Sigma_{\rm gas}$</tex>, within the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r < 2{}^{\prime\prime}$</tex> or 90 pc region reaches <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3.7 \times 10^3 M_\odot$</tex> pc<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-2}$</tex> if a Galactic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N_{\rm H_2}/I_{\rm CO}$</tex> conversion factor is applied. The extent of the central CO peak is about <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5{}^{\prime\prime}$</tex>, or 230 pc, and is elongated along the E-W direction with two-armed spiral-like structures, which are typical for barred disk galaxies. The HCN-to-CO integrated intensity ratio on the brightness temperature scale, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R_{\rm HCN/CO}$</tex>, is about 0.02 within the central <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r < 400$</tex> pc region. This <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R_{\rm HCN/CO}$</tex> is smaller than those in starburst regions by a factor of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5 \hbox{-} 15$</tex>. These molecular-gas properties would explain why NGC 5195 is in a post-starburst phase; most of the dense molecular cores (i.e., the very sites of massive star formation) have been consumed away by a past starburst event, and therefore a burst of massive star formation can no longer last, although a large amount of low density gas still exists. We find a steep rise of the rotation velocity toward the center of NGC 5195. As a consequence, the critical gas surface density for a local gravitational instability of the gas disk becomes very high (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Sigma_{\rm crit} \sim 6.9 \times 10^3 \,{{{M}_{\odot}}} \, {\rm pc}^{-2}$</tex>), suggesting that the molecular gas in the central region of NGC 5195 is gravitationally stable, in contrast to that of starburst galaxies. We propose that dense molecular gas can not be formed from remaining diffuse molecular gas because the molecular gas in the center of NGC 5195 is too stable to form dense cores via gravitational instabilities of diffuse molecular gas. The deduced very high threshold density seems to be due to a high mass concentration in NGC 5195. The known trends on the occurrence and luminosity of nuclear star formation in early-type galaxies can be understood naturally if the high threshold density is characteristic for early-type galaxies.

articleTitle: Effect of the Polarization of Photon Splitting on the Cyclotron Lines in Large-Scale Atmospheres with Super-Strong Magnetic Fields
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: The cyclotron lines are affected by photon splitting in super-strong magnetized atmospheres (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 4.4 \times 10^{13} \,{\rm G}$</tex>) into which a power-law-type flux is injected. We studied the polarization effect of photon splitting on the cyclotron line formation by treating different modes of splitting. We calculated the emergent spectra for two conditions: only one splitting mode and three splitting modes that could operate in a neutron-star atmosphere with a subcritical magnetic field. Photon splitting can also operate over a larger scale than cyclotron resonant scattering in a neutron-star atmosphere, since photon splitting occurs in a super-strong magnetic field even in the absence of a plasma. We therefore considered atmospheres consisting of lower and higher density regions. Cyclotron resonant scattering is dominant in a higher density region, and photon splitting is dominant in a lower density region. In three splitting modes, we found that the cyclotron absorption lines are strongly reprocessed by photon splitting, and thus may not be detected even for a magnetic field of about <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.0 \times 10^{13} \,{\rm G}$</tex> in the power-law-type spectra. However, we confirmed that the cyclotron absorption lines are not mostly reprocessed by photon splitting in only one splitting mode.

articleTitle: Excitation of Non-Axisymmetric g-Mode Oscillations by Corotation Resonance in Thin Relativistic Disks
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Various modes of oscillations are trapped in the inner region of geometrically thin relativistic disks. Among these oscillations, non-axisymmetric g-mode oscillations have been less studied compared with other modes of oscillations. The modes are, however, interesting since a corotation resonance appears in the trapped region. We mathematically examine whether the modes can be excited by the effects of the corotation resonance. This examination is made under an assumption that the inner and outer Lindblad radii are sufficiently separated in the opposite directions from the corotation radius. The results of analyses suggest that the waves are excited by the corotation resonance. The presence of the excitation suggests that the non-axisymmetric trapped g-mode oscillations are one of possible candidates for the quasi-periodic oscillations of a few hundred to kHz observed in some X-ray sources.

articleTitle: Near-Infrared Spectroscopy of Very Low-Luminosity Young Stellar Objects in the Taurus Molecular Cloud
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We carried out near-infrared spectroscopic observations of 23 very low-luminosity young stellar object (YSO) candidates and 5 of their companions in Heiles Cloud 2, one of the densest parts of the Taurus molecular cloud. Twelve objects were confirmed to be YSOs by the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm{B}\gamma$</tex> feature. The effective temperatures of the YSOs and of the companions are estimated from the 2.26-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mu \rm {m}}$</tex> feature, the 2.21-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mu \rm {m}}$</tex> feature, and the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm{H}_{2}\rm{O}$</tex> band strengths. Detailed comparisons of our photometric and spectroscopic observations with evolutionary tracks on the HR diagram suggest some objects to be very low-mass YSOs.

articleTitle: Properties of Spiral-Peculiar Type of Kiso Ultraviolet-Excess Galaxies
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We investigated the optical spectroscopic properties of 44 Kiso Ultraviolet-excess Galaxies (KUG), which is one of the most well-known catalogs of blue galaxies. All of our sample galaxies belong to the spiral-peculiar (Sp) type, the morphological class of spiral galaxy with a peculiar bar and/or a nucleus in KUGs. Since the Sp type is considered to be the most peculiar group among KUGs, and about 45% of the KUGs have the Sp type, a detailed study of the Sp type is crucial to understand the characteristics of the KUG. The sample galaxies have luminosities in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B$</tex>–band of about <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10^{8}$</tex> to less than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10^{10}$</tex> in solar unit, and a median physical size of 13 kpc. From the nuclear spectra, we determined line excitation sources in 39 galaxies. Among them, we detected four AGNs reliably: two Seyfert 1s, one Seyfert 2, and one LINER. Other sample galaxies show moderately star-forming activity. For this category of ordinary KUG group, the mode of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm{H}\alpha$</tex> equivalent width at the nuclear region is a bin of 40 to 60  Å. Three galaxies have extreme starburst nuclei with an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm{H}\alpha$</tex> equivalent width of more than 200  Å. The internal extinction of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_{V}$</tex> is about 0.8 mag, which suggests that the star-forming nuclei are not heavily enshrouded by dust.

articleTitle: A Multi-Band Photometric Study of Tidal Debris in a Compact Group of Galaxies: Seyfert’s Sextet
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: In order to investigate the properties of the prominent tidal debris feature extending to the northeast of a compact group of galaxies, Seyfert’s Sextet, we analyzed multi-band (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$VR$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K^{\prime }$</tex>) photometric imaging data and obtained the following results: 1) The radial surface brightness distribution of this tidal debris in Seyfert’s Sextet (TDSS) in each band appears to be well approximated by an exponential profile. 2) The observed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B-V$</tex> color of TDSS is similar to those of dwarf elliptical galaxies in nearby clusters. 3) Comparing the spectral energy distribution (SED) of TDSS with theoretical photometric evolution models and with the SED of the stars in the outer part of HCG 79b, we find that its SED is comparable to that of a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 10 \,\rm{Gyr}$</tex>-old stellar population with solar metallicity, similar to the stellar population in the outer part of HCG 79b. This suggests that TDSS consists of stars that may have been liberated from HCG 79b by strong galaxy interactions, not a pre-existing dwarf galaxy as previously thought.

articleTitle: Observations of SiO Maser Sources within a Few Parsec from the Galactic Center
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Mapping and monitoring observations of SiO maser sources near the Galactic center were made with the Nobeyama 45-m telescope at 43 GHz. Rectangular mapping an area of approximately <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$200^{\prime\prime} \times 100^{\prime\prime}$</tex> in a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${30{}^{\rm {\prime \prime }}}$</tex> grid, and triangular mapping in a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${20{}^{\rm {\prime \prime }}}$</tex> grid toward the Galactic center, resulted in 15 detections of SiO sources; the positions of the sources were obtained with errors of 5 – <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${10{}^{\rm {\prime \prime }}}$</tex> , except for a few weak sources. Three-year monitoring observations found that the component at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{\rm lsr} =-27 \,{\rm km} \, {\rm s}^{-1}$</tex> of IRS 10 EE flared to about 1.5 Jy during 2000 March–May, which was a factor of more than 5 brighter than its normal intensity. Using the radial velocities and positions of the SiO sources, we identified 5 which are counterparts of previously observed OH 1612 MHz sources. The other 10 SiO sources have no OH counterparts, but two were previously detected with VLA, and four are located close to the positions of large-amplitude variables observed at near-infrared wavelengths. A least-squares fit to a plot of velocities versus Galactic longitudes gives a rather high speed for the rotation of the star cluster around the Galactic center. The observed radial-velocity dispersion is roughly consistent with a value obtained before. It was found that all of the SiO sources with OH 1612 MHz counterparts have periods of light variation longer than 450 days, while SiO sources without OH masers often have periods shorter than 450 days. This fact suggests that lower-mass AGB stars are more often detected in SiO masers than in the OH 1612 MHz line.

articleTitle: Reliability of Merger Tree Realizations of Dark Halos in the Monte Carlo Modeling of Galaxy Formation
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We examine the reliability of the merger trees generated for the Monte Carlo modeling of galaxy formation. In particular we focus on the cold gas fraction predicted from merger trees with different assumptions on the progenitor distribution function, the timestep, and the mass resolution. We show that the cold gas fraction is sensitive to the accuracy of the merger trees at small-mass scales of progenitors at high redshifts. One can reproduce the Press–Schechter prediction to a reasonable degree by adopting a fairly large number of redshift bins, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N_{\rm step}\sim 1000$</tex>, in generating merger trees, which is a factor of ten larger than the canonical value used in previous literature.

articleTitle: A New Empirical Method for Estimating the Far-Infrared Flux of Galaxies
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We propose a new empirical method to estimate the total far-infrared flux of galaxies from the spectral energy distribution (SED) at wavelengths of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda \leq 100 \, {\mu \rm {m}}$</tex>. It is difficult to derive the total far-infrared luminosity from only the IRAS data, though it is one of the most important properties of galaxies. Observations by Infrared Telescope in Space (IRTS) indicate that the SED of the diffuse emission from the Galactic plane in this wavelength region can be derived from the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$60 \, {\mu \rm {m}}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$100 \, {\mu \rm {m}}$</tex> color. This empirical SED relation was improved in order to obtain a better fit to the Galactic plane data for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I_\nu(60 \, {\mu \rm {m}}) / I_\nu(100 \, {\mu \rm {m}}) \gt 0.6$</tex>, and applied to 96 IRAS galaxies for which ISOPHOT and KAO data are available at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda \gt 100 \, {\mu \rm {m}}$</tex>. As a result, the empirical relation well describes the far-infrared (FIR) SED for a majority of galaxies. Additionally, the total FIR flux for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda \geq 40 \, {\mu \rm {m}}$</tex> was derived from the flux densities at 60 and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$100 \, {\mu \rm {m}}$</tex> by using this model. For the 96 IRAS galaxies, the uncertainty in the total far-infrared flux of the present method is 26%. The present method is more accurate than the previous one widely used to derive the total infrared flux from the IRAS 60 and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$100 \, {\mu \rm {m}}$</tex> data.

articleTitle: Evolution of Hard X-Ray Radiation from Clusters of Galaxies: Bremsstrahlung or Inverse Compton Scattering?
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We have calculated the evolution of a non-thermal electron population from super-thermal (but weakly relativistic) to highly relativistic energy range in clusters of galaxies. We investigate the evolution of hard X-ray radiation due to both bremsstrahlung and inverse Compton scattering of the cosmic microwave background photons. The bremsstrahlung component is more significant than that of inverse Compton scattering when the momentum spectra of the electron sources are steeper than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim P_{\rm e}^{-3.0}$</tex> and vice versa in the case of Coma, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P_{\rm e}$</tex> is the electron momentum. The resultant hard X-ray spectra are flatter when the bremsstrahlung component is dominant. When the spectral indices of the source term are in the intermediate range (from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-2.5$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-3.5$</tex>), too much extreme ultraviolet emission is produced. Inverse-Compton-dominant models can reproduce Coma cluster results with reasonable injection rates, which are possible in cluster mergers and/or ambient gas accretion.

articleTitle: Optical Observations of XTE J1118 + 480 during the 2000 Outburst
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report on photometric and spectroscopic observations of a possible halo black-hole X-ray nova, XTE J1118<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+$</tex>480 (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$=$</tex> KV UMa) during outburst. Our photometric monitoring during the main outburst revealed that the optical maximum as well as the onset of the outburst precede those in the X-ray region. This indicates that the event was an “outside-in” type outburst and that its optical flux was dominated by viscous heating, itself, and not the effect of X-ray irradiation. Based on these results, we suggest an outburst scenario analogous to superoutbursts in SU UMa-type dwarf novae. This scenario predicts a superhump phenomenon, which we indeed detected throughout the outburst. We determined its period to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.170529\pm 0.000006 \,{\rm d}$</tex>, which is slightly longer than the orbital periods suggested from spectroscopic observations. We have furthermore revealed the first evidence of a continuous period decreasing in X-ray novae. The most prominent feature in our optical spectrum is a double-peak He II 4686Å emission line having an asymmetric profile with an outstanding blue side peak. Using a Doppler mapping method, we found that the He II emission originates from the accretion disk, which particularly concentrates on the hot spot. The time that the blue peak becomes strongest corresponds to a superhump peak. This implies that we see an elongated side of an eccentric disk at that time and, hence, it may cause an asymmetric emission profile. Substituting the observed fractional superhump excess for a theoretically expected relation between it and the mass ratio, we estimate that the black-hole mass is larger than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$9.5 \,{{{M}_{\odot}}}$</tex>. XTE J1118<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+$</tex>480 thus has a large mass of a compact object compared with the typical black-hole X-ray novae.

articleTitle: Superhump Evolution in the Ultrashort Period Dwarf Nova 1RXS J232953.9+062814
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report on the evolution of superhumps and late superhumps in an ultrashort period dwarf nova, 1RXS J232953.9<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+$</tex>062814, during the superoutburst in 2001 November. Ordinary superhumps were observed throughout a plateau phase, a rapid fading phase, and a rebrightening phase. During the plateau phase, the superhump period increased with time at a large rate of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P_{\rm dot} = 1.19 \pm 0.24 \times 10^{-4}$</tex>. In conjunction with the rebrightening phenomenon, these characteristics indicate that an accretion disk expanded further outward from the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3:1$</tex> resonance radius, which caused a large amount of left over matter at the outer disk, even after the superoutburst. In the post-outburst phase, we detected late superhumps superimposed on dominant double-peak modulations. Late superhumps were observed at least for 10 d without a significant period change. We detected the first normal outburst of this object on 2001 December 26. The interval between the superoutburst and this normal one is 53 d. This short recurrence time supports a high mass-transfer rate in this system. Concerning the evolutionary status of 1RXS J232953.9<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+$</tex>062814, we propose that it is a progenitor of AM CVn stars on the evolutionary course of the cataclysmic variable channel in which systems have a secondary star with a hydrogen-exhausted core.

articleTitle: Near-Infrared Observations of the IRAS/SiO Sources in the Galactic Bulge: a Large Scale Distribution
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Near-infrared photometric observations in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J$</tex>-, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H$</tex>-, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex>-bands were made for 120 IRAS sources toward the Galactic bulge (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-10^{\circ} < l < 15^{\circ}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\vert b\vert < 3^{\circ}$</tex>, excluding <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\vert l\vert < 3^{\circ}$</tex>). They are well-confirmed, mass-losing late-type stars having accurate radial velocities derived from SiO maser observations. For 118 sources, single, unambiguous near-infrared counterparts were found within the errors of the IRAS/MSX positions; and for the other 2 sources, faint candidates only detectable in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex>-band were found. From the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J$</tex>-, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H$</tex>-, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex>-band and IRAS 12 and 25<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\, {\mu \rm {m}}$</tex> intensities, we estimated the spectral energy distributions of the sources, and obtained distances assuming a constant intrinsic luminosity. Adding all of the distance data of the IRAS/SiO sources in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-10^{\circ} < l < 25^{\circ}$</tex> published in previous papers, we mapped the positions of 272 sampled stars onto the Galactic plane. The map clearly shows a bar structure, where the major axis of the bar is oriented <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$22^{\circ}(\pm 8^{\circ}$</tex>) from the Sun-Galactic center line. We also reanalyzed the radial-velocity shift with the distance in this sample. These analyses suggest that the data are consistent with the current bar theory of the Galactic bulge.

articleTitle: Chemical Composition of Carbon-Rich, Very Metal-Poor Subgiant LP 625-44 Observed with the Subaru/HDS
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We have obtained high-resolution (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R\sim 90000$</tex>) spectra of the carbon-and s-process-element-rich, very metal-poor (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm{[Fe/H]} =-2.7$</tex>) subgiant LP 625-44, as well as those of HD 140283 (a metal-poor subgiant with normal abundance ratio) for a comparison, with the High Dispersion Spectrograph (HDS) for the Subaru Telescope for detailed abundance study. The excess of oxygen in LP 625-44 seems to be remarkable (perhaps by nearly a factor 10) compared with that of HD 140283 derived from the O i triplet around 7770 Å, though the oxygen abundance derived from these lines is uncertain. The Na enhancement in LP 625-44 is by about a factor 50, suggesting hydrogen burning in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{22\atop} \rm{Ne}}$</tex>-rich layer in an asymptotic giant branch star which produced the abundance pattern of this object. In our new spectrum of LP 625-44, the Pb i<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda$</tex>3683 Å line has been detected, confirming the Pb abundance [<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\log \epsilon \rm{(Pb)} \sim 1.9$</tex>] derived from the Pb i<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda$</tex>4057 Å line by previous work. The abundance ratio of s-process elements at the second peak (e.g., La, Ce, and Nd) to that at the third peak (Pb) in LP 625-44 is significantly higher (by a factor 5) than that in other three s-process element-rich objects recently studied by van Eck et al. Recent theoretical studies have modeled s-process nucleosynthesis in the radiative layer of asymptotic giant branch stars in the inter-pulse phase. The above results mean that these processes produced a large scatter in the abundance ratios, or different processes (e.g., s-process nucleosynthesis during thermal pulses) contributed to heavy elements in the early Galaxy.

articleTitle: Iodine-Cell Spectroscopy at Okayama Astrophysical Observatory: First Results
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Toward the aims of spectroscopically searching for planetary systems around stars, or detecting oscillations of solar-type stars for stellar seismology, we have started an experimental project of very precise determinations of stellar radial velocity variations based on the iodine-cell (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm{I}_{2}$</tex> cell) technique at Okayama Astrophysical Observatory. We here report on the first preliminary results of test observations for two planet-harboring stars (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\upsilon $</tex> And and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tau $</tex> Boo) based on data obtained by using the newly developed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm{I}_{2}$</tex> cell and processed with a practical and quick analysis method. We confirmed that the internal statistical error can be as small as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5 \hbox{-} 6 \,\rm{m} \,\rm{s}^{-1}$</tex> at best. Then, the resulting radial velocity solutions turned out to be in reasonable agreement with the well-established predicted variations over a time span of 4–5 days; the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$O-C$</tex> deviations indicate that a short-time-scale precision of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 15\,\rm{m} \,\rm{s}^{-1}$</tex> has been accomplished in a practical sense.

articleTitle: 3-D Kinematics of Water Masers in the W 51A Region
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report on proper-motion measurements of water masers in the massive-star forming region W 51A and analyses of the 3-D kinematics of the masers in three maser clusters of W 51A (W 51 North, Main, and South). In W 51 North, we found a clear expanding flow having an expansion velocity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 70 \,\rm{km} \,\rm{s}^{-1}$</tex>, which indicates deceleration. The originating point of the flow coincides within <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${0\rlap {.}{}^{\rm {\prime \prime }}1}$</tex> with a silicon-monoxide maser source near the H II region W 51d. In W 51 Main, no systematic motion was found over the whole velocity range (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$- 58 \,{\rm km} \,{\rm s}^{-1} \leq V_{\rm{LSR}} < 158 \,{\rm km} \,{\rm s}^{-1}$</tex>), although a stream motion was previously reported in a limited range of the Doppler velocity (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$54 \,{\rm km} \,{\rm s}^{-1} \leq V_{\rm{LSR}} < 68 \,{\rm km} \,{\rm s}^{-1}$</tex>). Multiple driving sources of outflows are thought to explain the kinematics of W 51 Main. In W 51 South, an expansion motion like a bipolar flow was marginally visible. Analyses based on diagonalization of the variance–covariance matrix of maser velocity vectors demonstrate that the maser kinematics in W 51 North and Main are significantly tri-axially asymmetric. We estimated the distance to W 51 North to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$6.1 \pm 1.3 \,{\rm kpc}$</tex> based on a model-fitting method adopting a radially expanding flow.

Author Keywords: ISM: individual objects (W 51A, W 51 North, W 51 Main, W 51 South)

articleTitle: Interstellar Gas Mass Functions: Fractality and Scale Dependence
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present a theoretical model for the observed mass functions (MF’s) of interstellar clouds, and test it by comparison with interferometrically observed MF’s. We consider the time evolution of velocities using the stochastic differential Langevin equation for the objects (in fact gas clumps of sizes below 1 pc) under Brownian motion, with friction and magnetic field. We also study geometrical binding, and hence the implications of sizes of the regions in which the gas clouds move, and also of the departures from sphericity of the clouds themselves. The size of the global region in which the objects move under the influence of the general dynamics of the galaxy leads to a box-effect modelled as a Chandrasekhar barrier, which naturally leads to the superposition of Gaussian distributions over different ranges of displacement, and with progressively decreasing amplitude. This accounts for the general power law trend observed for the MF’s, as well as its accompanying peaked structure. These results fit well the observed distributions even in very low mass ranges, which show global power law characteristics (scale independence, fractality, departures from sphericity for individual clouds), accompanied by turnovers, for a wide range of masses, characteristics of Gaussians (scale dependence, a tendency for clouds to be spherical).

articleTitle: High Dispersion Spectrograph (HDS) for the Subaru Telescope
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present the design and performance of the High Dispersion Spectrograph (HDS) of the Subaru Telescope. HDS is an echelle spectrograph located at the Nasmyth focus of the telescope. The collimated beam size is 272 mm, and the echelle is 300 mm by 840 mm in total size (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$31.6 \,{\rm gr} \,{\rm mm}^{-1}, R=2.8$</tex>). HDS has two cross-dispersing gratings with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$400 \,{\rm gr} \,{\rm mm}^{-1}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$250 \,{\rm gr} \,{\rm mm}^{-1}$</tex>, which are optimized for the blue and red wavelength regions, respectively. The camera is of the catadioptric type system, consisting of three corrector lenses and a mirror. Two EEV-CCD’s with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4100 \times 2048$</tex> pixels and a pixel size of 13.5 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mu \rm {m}}$</tex> are used as the detector. A standard configuration with a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${0\rlap {.}{}^{\rm {\prime \prime }}4}$</tex> slit gives a spectral resolution of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R=90000$</tex>, and a narrower slit width enables higher resolution of up to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R \sim 160000$</tex>. The spectrograph has sensitivities from 3000 Å to 1 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mu {\rm m}}$</tex>, and one exposure covers a range of 1500–2500 Å, depending on the wavelength region. The throughput of the telescope and the spectrograph, including the efficiency of the detector, is about 13% in 5000–6000 Å and about 8% at 4000 Å. The stability of the spectrograph and scattered light level are also reported.

articleTitle: Detection of Zinc in the Very Metal-Poor Post-AGB Star HR 4049
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report on the detection of two Zn i lines at 4722.15 Å and 4810.53 Å in the high-quality spectrum of the very metal-poor post-AGB star HR 4049, which was obtained with the High Dispersion Spectrograph attached to the Subaru Telescope. The strengths of these lines indicate an appreciable underabundance of Zn by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim-1.3 \,{\rm dex}$</tex> relative to the Sun. The fact that this volatile element, similarly to others belonging to the same group (e.g., C, N, O, S), does not conform to the extreme depletion (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gt 4 \,{\rm dex}$</tex>) of refractory metals (e.g., Fe), strongly suggests that grain formation has something to do with the origin of the chemical peculiarity. This (not extremely but significantly) subsolar value of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm{[Zn/H]}$</tex> is quantitatively discussed in connection with those of other volatile species, especially with respect to S. We also detected a new Fe ii line at 5159.03 Å along with the already known Fe ii 4923.93 Å line; based on these two lines the Fe abundance of HR 4049 is determined to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 2.8$</tex> (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm{[Fe/H]} \sim-4.7$</tex>).

articleTitle: Spectroscopic Studies of the Solar Corona II. Properties of Green and Red Emission Lines in Open and Closed Coronal Structures
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We obtained profiles of the green (Fe XIV 5303 Å) and red (Fe X 6374 Å) emission lines simultaneously on 1998 July 18–19 for about 4 hours with a cadence of 10 minutes, covering an area of about <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$200'' \times 500''$</tex> in the solar corona. The line width (FWHM), intensity, and Doppler shift for both lines were computed using Gaussian fits to the observed line profiles. We then studied any systematic differences in these parameters between closed and open field structures, and their time variations. The derived line widths indicate that the FWHM of the red line increases with height above the limb at a rate of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.5 \hbox{-} 2.6 \,\rm{m}$</tex> Å<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\,\rm{arcsec}^{-1}$</tex> and the green-line width decreases with height at a rate of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.2 \hbox{-} 3.4 \,\rm{m}$</tex> Å<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\,\rm{arcsec}^{-1}$</tex>. The difference in the time-averaged values of the widths of the green line in open and closed coronal structures at a given height above the limb is small, whereas the width of the red line in open structures is substantially larger than that in the closed loop-like coronal structures.

articleTitle: FOCAS: The Faint Object Camera and Spectrograph for the Subaru Telescope
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: The Faint Object Camera and Spectrograph (FOCAS) is a Cassegrain optical instrument for the Subaru Telescope. Its capabilities include <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$6^\prime \phi$</tex> FOV direct imaging, low-resolution spectroscopy (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R=250 \hbox{-} 2000$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${0\rlap {.}{}^{\rm {\prime \prime }}4}$</tex> slitwidth), multi-slit spectroscopy and polarimetry. We describe the overall design of FOCAS, its observing functions, and the performance verification procedures that have been carried out.

articleTitle: Development of Iodine Cells for the Subaru HDS and the Okayama HIDES: II. New Software for Precise Radial Velocity Measurements
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We have developed a computer code for precise measurements of stellar radial velocity variations with iodine (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm{I}_2$</tex>) cells attached to the High Dispersion Spectrograph (HDS) on Subaru Telescope and the HIgh Dispersion Echelle Spectrograph (HIDES) on Okayama 188 cm reflector. Our modeling technique for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm{I}_2$</tex> data is similar to those described by Butler et al. (, AAA 65.036.447) and Valenti et al. (, AAA 64.036.209) concerning the point that the stellar spectrum taken through the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm{I}_2$</tex> cell (star<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+ \rm{I}_2$</tex> spectrum) is modeled as the product of high-resolution stellar and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rm{I}_2$</tex> template spectra convolved with the modeled instrumental profile (IP) of the spectrograph. In order to generate a template stellar spectrum, we have devised a new method to extract an intrinsic stellar spectrum from observed star<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+ \rm{I}_2$</tex> spectra. This enables us to obtain a well-established template stellar spectrum even in cases when the IP and the wavelength scale are apt to vary with time and the observational conditions, and the existing method which reconstructs the IP from a B-star<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+ \rm{I}_2$</tex> spectrum (Butler et al. 1996; Endl et al. 2000, A&A, 362, 585) fails. We here report on the results of our Doppler measurements of three solar-type stars, 16 Cyg B, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tau$</tex> Cet, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\upsilon$</tex> And, based on data collected with HDS and HIDES for about one year. These results show that we have achieved a precision of about <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5 \hbox{-} 6 \,\rm{m} \,\rm{s}^{-1}$</tex> over a time span of one year with our current analysis package with both spectrographs.

Author Keywords: stars: individual (16 Cyg B, τ Cet, υ And)
